Region: The southwestern coastal plain around Gaza, in unwalled settlements (Hazerim)
History: The Avvim dwelt in Hazerim, unwalled villages, on the coastal plain toward Gaza, until the Caphtorim came out of Caphtor, destroyed them, and dwelt in their place (Deuteronomy 2:23). Joshua 13:3 still counts the Avvim among the land yet to be taken, listed beside the five lords of the Philistines, a sign that a remnant remained into the conquest era.
Culture: Villagers of the coastal plain, living in unwalled settlements rather than fortified cities, which left them exposed to the Caphtorim who displaced them.
BibleConnection: The Avvim are a small, displaced people of the coast: an example in Deuteronomy 2 of how peoples rose and fell in the land before Israel ever arrived.
